bib.title: The Markovian Thinker: Architecture-Agnostic Linear Scaling of Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "The Markovian Thinker: Architecture-Agnostic Linear Scaling of Reasoning". Aghajohari*, Chitsaz*, Kazemnejad*, Chandar, Sordoni, Courville, Reddy (Mila, Microsoft Research, McGill, ServiceNow). arXiv:2510.06557v3, 13 Nov 2025. Preprint. Code and weights are released (McGill-NLP).

COVERAGE: FULL. I read all 2009 lines (111,581 chars, 34 pages) of /tmp/potw-aghajohari-2025-markovian-thinker.txt, including the references and appendices A-J. Figure axis numbers were garbled in places but the captions and tables were intact. I did not run figures.py. I did not check the extraction against the PDF.

CENTRAL CLAIM: Standard RL for reasoning models uses an environment whose state is the prompt plus all prior reasoning tokens. That makes the state unbounded and compute quadratic in thinking length. Delethink changes the environment. Reasoning runs in fixed-size chunks, and at each boundary the context is reset to the query plus the last m tokens of the previous chunk. RL teaches the model to write a textual state near the end of each chunk. Per the paper, thinking length is decoupled from context size, giving linear compute and constant memory with no architecture change.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Delethink 24K matches or beats LongCoT-RL 24K on math at the same total thinking budget.
 number: Delethink 24K / LongCoT-RL 24K / LongCoT-RL 8K / base. AIME24 0.46 / 0.40 / 0.35 / 0.29; AIME25 0.35 / 0.30 / 0.28 / 0.24; HMMT25 0.21 / 0.18 / 0.15 / 0.15 (read off the Fig 4 bar labels in extraction order; the labels are ambiguous, and some are shaded test-time-scaling gains, so verify against the figure).
 setup: R1-Distill 1.5B, DeepScaleR (about 40K problems), C=8K, m=C/2=4K, I=5, so 8K+(5-1)x4K=24K. GRPO, 1000 steps, 128 prompts x 8 traces per step, lr 1e-6, KL off, temperature 0.6. Best checkpoint chosen on AIME24, which is also a reported benchmark. Accuracy is avg@128 by bootstrap from 256 samples, std below 0.004.
 quote: "LongCoT-RL 8K underperforms Delethink by 5.5% (Figure 4)". Also: "Delethink attains higher scores than LongCoT-RL 24K on AIME'24, AIME'25, and HMMT'25."
 where: Sec 6 and 6.1, p.9-10.
2. Out-of-distribution gains are modest.
 number: GPQA-Diamond and LiveCodeBench; Fig 4 labels give 0.36 vs 0.35 and 0.23 vs 0.21 (the label order is unclear).
 quote: "gains are modest; nevertheless, Delethink matches or slightly surpasses LongCoT-RL 24K."
 where: Sec 6.1, Fig 4 caption.
3. Training cost at long thinking lengths.
 number: 27 vs 7 H100-months.
 setup: an estimate, not a measured run. Time of one RL step was measured at assumed average thinking lengths of 16K-96K (verl+SGLang, H100s, R1-Distill 1.5B) and extrapolated to the full run. The abstract says 96K and the intro and Fig 2 text say 94K; the paper is inconsistent.
 quote: "we empirically estimate at 96K average thinking length LongCoT-RL costs 27 H100-months vs. 7 for Delethink."
 where: Abstract p.1, Fig 2c p.3.
4. Measured per-step cost at 24K.
 number: 215s vs 248.5s per RL step; 8,500 vs 6,000 tokens/s per H100; generation 130s vs 170s; backward 80s vs 70s.
 setup: Delethink vs LongCoT-RL 24K, 8xH100, no sequence parallelism.
 quote: "Delethink completes each RL step in 215s, faster than LongCoT-RL 24K at 248.5s. Its token generation is also more efficient, reaching 8,500 tokens per second per H100 versus 6,000 for LongCoT-RL 24K."
 where: Sec 6.3, p.10.
 Note: backward is slower for Delethink at this length. The authors attribute this to constant and lower-order terms.
5. FLOP crossover and savings.
 number: crossover at about 30K tokens; 17x FLOP reduction at 1M tokens.
 setup: computed in closed form for the R1-Distill 1.5B architecture, C=8K, m=4K, 1000 episodes. This is theory, not a measured run.
 quote: "Below 32K tokens, Delethink can be slower since non-attention blocks dominate, but beyond that point, the quadratic scaling of attention makes Delethink increasingly faster. At one million tokens, Delethink achieves 17x reduction in FLOPs."
 where: Sec 6.3, App C, Fig 3, Fig C.1.
 The cause of the crossover: each token is generated once and then re-encoded as the next chunk's prompt, so non-attention cost doubles.
6. Scaling laws given (Table, p.5).
 Delethink: FLOP O(n^2 S), memory O(n), backward O(T_B S), generation O(T_G S).
 LongCoT: FLOP O(n^2 S^2), memory O(nS), backward O(T_B S^2), generation O(T_G S^2).
 Throughput is proportional to 1/L, after Ao et al. 2025 (App B).
 quote: "LongCoT's throughput falls by a factor of S, scaling time by S^2. Delethink's throughput is constant, so its time scales only as S."
 Effect of C and m: C=2n gives O(4n^2 S); C=n with m=n/4 gives O(4/3 n^2 S).
7. KV-cache and memory.
 number: a 1M-token trace on a 1.5B model fills one H100.
 setup: R1-Distill 1.5B; stated, with no calculation shown.
 quote: "the KV cache of a 1M-token trace on R1-Distill 1.5B, a small model, alone fills an entire H100."
 where: Sec 4.3, p.8.
 Delethink keeps only the current chunk's cache.
 Fig 4b: throughput stays flat for Delethink, while LongCoT declines as thinking grows from 16K to 96K. Values are plotted on a 0-7500 tokens/s axis and are not tabulated beyond claim 4.
8. KV handling at a chunk boundary.
 quote: "the KV cache must be cleared at this point and the carryover tokens will be re-encoded as part of the new prefix. This adds an O(m^2) encoding cost at each boundary... the prefill operation is quite fast compared to decoding in modern inference engine."
 where: Sec 4.1, p.6.
 No prefix-cache reuse is claimed. The carryover is re-encoded under the query, so its KV differs.
9. Test-time scaling beyond the trained budget.
 number: Delethink keeps improving to 128K; LongCoT-RL 24K and 8K plateau at their training limits. Some AIME25 problems are solved only after up to 140K thinking tokens.
 setup: sequential Pass@1, not majority@k. Trained at 24K, tested to 128K. Traces right-trimmed to the budget.
 quote: "Delethink continues to improve even when reasoning with 100K more tokens than it encountered during training."
 where: Sec 6.2, Figs 2b and 7.
10. 96K scaling run.
 number: 49% on AIME24 with solutions averaging 36K tokens; mean trace length reaches 36K (AIME24) and 42K (AIME25).
 setup: C=8K, I=23. Initialized from the Delethink-24K checkpoint, then 150 steps on OpenMath. Compared to a Delethink-24K model evaluated at a 128K budget.
 quote: "Despite the short training schedule, Delethink 96K not only surpasses the base performance of Delethink 24K checkpoint, but also matches or exceeds a test-time-scaled Delethink 24K evaluated with a 128K token budget."
 where: Sec 6.5, Fig 8.
 The authors call these results "preliminary". No LongCoT-RL 96K baseline was trained: "we could not train the latter under our compute resources" (App C).
11. Zero-shot Markovian behaviour at RL initialisation (Delethink tracing with no training or prompting).
 R1-Distill 1.5B, 7B and 14B: C=8K recovers LongCoT performance across tasks. C=4K trails only on GPQA. Zero-shot Delethink also beats LongCoT on AIME at large budgets.
 Zero-shot Table G.2 (avg@128, %), LongCoT 32k vs Delethink. These are run on the base models. They show LongCoT 32k vs Delethink tracing, not a trained model.
 - 1.5B: AIME24 29.3 vs 37.2; AIME25 23.6 vs 29.5; GPQA 33.9 vs 34.6; LCB 19.2 vs 19.9.
 - 7B: AIME24 54.4 vs 64.1; AIME25 40.5 vs 47.1; GPQA 50.7 vs 50.2; LCB 37.9 vs 39.7.
 - 14B: AIME24 68.9 vs 71.8; AIME25 52.8 vs 52.5; GPQA 55.6 vs 57.5; LCB 51.5 vs 52.2.
 GPT-OSS 120B and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking: C=16K "matches or exceeds LongCoT on Qwen3 and almost matches on GPT-OSS." C=8K "has a lower test-time scaling slope and lags behind LongCoT."
 Problem coverage on GPQA-Diamond: GPT-OSS solves 161 with Delethink vs 159 with LongCoT; Qwen3 solves 138 with both. AIME coverage is nearly identical.
 where: Sec 7, Figs 9-11, Table G.2.
12. Chunk size ablation (trained), Fig 6.
 C=8K and 4K perform similarly; C=2K trails but still improves over the base model. Total budget held at about 24K, m=C/2. Validation is AIME24 avg@32.
 where: Sec 6.4.
13. State size m ablation (zero-shot, App E, Fig E.3).
 At C=8K, R1-Distill accuracy is "essentially flat" for m from 1K to 7K. Qwen3-30B-A3B depends strongly on m, with larger m better. At C=4K the R1 family also shows a dependence on m.
 I values used: I={6,7,8,10,13,19,37} for m={1k..7k}, via Tmax=C+(I-1)(C-m).
 C=2K: models almost never emit EOS within budget (Fig E.6). Authors' explanation: positional embedding reset and bias toward continuation.
14. Stress test on CrossWordBench (Fig 11).
 Delethink is comparable to LongCoT on 7x7 puzzles. On 14x14 puzzles performance declines relative to LongCoT. Labels in the extraction (one set per model): 77.4/31.3/77.5/61.7 and 32.2/19.7/32.7/24.2. Which number belongs to which method and size is not recoverable from the extraction, so check the figure.
 quote: "On the more challenging 14x14 puzzles, performance declines relative to LongCoT, though both models continue to produce a nontrivial number of valid Markovian traces."
15. Budget forcing (s1-style "Wait") hurts R1-distill.
 On AIME24 with the 1.5B model, forcing raised the average length from about 17k to 25k tokens while accuracy dropped (Fig G.8). Table G.2 shows Budget Force below LongCoT 32k for the 1.5B and 7B models, and mixed for the 14B.
 Relevance: reasoning-length angle.
16. Delethink tracing applied to a LongCoT-RL 24K checkpoint with no extra training.
 Accuracy rises nearly 4%, "almost as much as the gain it achieved from its entire RL training". Fig F.7 uses AIME25 and HMMT25. The effect vanishes when queries are kept under 16K (the "infinite budget illusion" hypothesis). Held-out AIME25 for the accuracy; the "nearly 4%" is not tied to a specific C.

LIMITS
- Trained only one model, R1-Distill 1.5B, on math only. For larger models it only shows zero-shot (step zero) results. Authors: "Training larger models is not possible within our compute budget."
- The 96K run is short (150 steps) and is called preliminary. It has no LongCoT-RL 96K comparison.
- Best checkpoint is selected on AIME24, which is also reported. One seed is implied; no variance across training runs is reported. The std below 0.004 is only evaluation bootstrap noise.
- The cost figures of 27 vs 7 H100-months are estimates extrapolated from single-step timings. Backward is slower than LongCoT at 24K, and FLOPs are higher below about 30K tokens.
- Out-of-distribution gains are small. CrossWordBench shows a weaker result on 14x14 puzzles. The 8K chunk is weaker zero-shot for GPT-OSS and Qwen3. C=2K fails to terminate.
- KV cache is cleared at every boundary. No KV-state MDP is built: "current systems (e.g., SGLang, Hugging Face Transformers, FSDP) do not provide this."
- Why it works is hypothesis ("speculative"): short-context pretraining, human reasoning being roughly Markovian, more abstract reasoning. These are not tested.
- The authors concede that "This could never work in areas like long-context retrieval."
- A claim in 6.2 that traces went to 140K points to Section H, which plots only AIME25 per-problem; it is a sample, not a general result.
- Sequential scaling only. Parallel scaling (majority@k, pass@k) is not compared.
- Delethink and LongCoT share a clip-high sweep tuned for LongCoT; Delethink reuses it.
- The paper's tables and figure labels show the LongCoT 24K baseline from its own recipe, not a published checkpoint.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Environment and RLVR: Lambert et al. 2024 (Tulu 3); Kazemnejad et al. 2025 (VinePPO); GRPO from Shao et al. 2024; REINFORCE from Williams 1992; policy gradient from Sutton et al. 1999.
- Training recipe: DeepScaleR (Luo et al. 2025b); DAPO (Yu et al. 2025) for KL off and clip-high; truncated importance sampling from Yao et al. 2025; verl (Sheng et al. 2024); SGLang (Zheng et al. 2024); FSDP (Zhao et al. 2023).
- Base models: DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al. 2025); gpt-oss (Agarwal et al. 2025); Qwen3 (Yang et al. 2025).
- Throughput model: Ao et al. 2025 (fluid-guided scheduling with memory constraints).
- Closest prior method: InftyThink (Yan et al. 2025), which iteratively summarises and is fixed by hand-crafted distilled data; Delethink learns the state through RL. Also TrimR (Lin et al. 2025), LIMOPro (Xiao et al. 2025).
- KV-cache work named: StreamingLLM attention sinks (Xiao et al. 2024), H2O (Zhang et al. 2023), Double Sparsity (Yang et al. 2024a), KVQuant (Hooper et al. 2024), KIVI (Liu et al. 2024b), learned eviction (Lancucki et al. 2025).
- Non-quadratic architectures: Katharopoulos et al. 2020, Yang et al. 2024b (GLA), Gu & Dao 2023 (Mamba), Longformer (Beltagy et al. 2020), BigBird (Zaheer et al. 2020), Jamba (Lieber et al. 2024).
- Length-control RL: L1 (Aggarwal & Welleck 2025), ThinkPrune (Hou et al. 2025), DAST, O1-Pruner, S-GRPO, multi-stage RL (Luo et al. 2025b), and Zeng et al. 2025 (GLM-4.5), which found multi-stage RL hurts.
- Budget forcing from s1, which the paper attributes to Guo et al. 2025 (this attribution is as printed).

CODE (verbatim, Fig C.2, p.24)
```
C, m, I, T = 8192, 4096, 5, 0.6 # chunk context, markovian tail, iteration cap, temperature
...
max_new = C if it == 0 else (C - m)
...
if it == 0:
    # Fold the first hundered tokens of the first chunk into query
    query_ids = query_ids + response_ids[:100]
...
prompt_ids = query_ids + response_ids[-m:]
```
Algorithm 1 (p.4): x <- q (+) y_{-m:}; generate up to C-m tokens; loop up to I-1 times; stop at EOS. Max thinking tokens = C + (I-1)(C-m) (Sec 4.1).
Memory/throughput (App B): M* = n*(l + l'/2); T* = n*/(d0 + d1 n*(l + l'/2)); throughput proportional to 1/l' when l' >> l.
Hyperparameters (Table D.1): prompt/response length 2,048/8,192 (Delethink) vs 2,048/24,576 (LongCoT); clip 0.20/0.26; lr 1e-6; loss aggregation trace-length batch mean vs seq-mean batch mean.

FIGURES (page numbers from extraction order; not verified against the PDF)
- Fig 1 (p.2): chunked vs growing context. Fastest explanation of the method.
- Fig 2 (p.3): (a) RL curve, (b) test-time scaling to 128K, (c) training cost H100 hours vs thinking tokens, quadratic vs linear. Best single summary of the cost claim.
- Fig 3 and Table (p.5): FLOP profile to 1M tokens (non-attention, attention, total) and the scaling table.
- Fig 4 (p.6): task bars, plus per-GPU throughput 16K-96K.
- Fig 7 (p.9): test-time scaling curves beyond the trained budget.
- Fig 8 (p.10): 96K scaling.
- Fig 9 and Fig 10 (p.11-12): zero-shot Delethink tracing on R1-Distill, GPT-OSS, Qwen3.
- Fig C.1 (p.23): FLOP crossover near 30K.
- Fig E.6 (p.28): C=2K failure to terminate.
- Fig J.12 (p.34): full attention vs sliding window vs streaming vs Delethink KV reset. Useful for the KV-cache note.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The extraction mangles the numbers in plot axes and the bar labels in Fig 4 and Fig 11, so those were not quoted as precise results; check them against the PDF if used. The abstract says 96K for the cost comparison while the intro says 94K. The paper writes "Section H" for the 140K example. Page numbers are inferred from the extraction. I did not run figures.py.
